newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas drifts lower ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas drifts lower ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices moved lower Friday ahead of the weekend as more moderate temperatures were forecast for early next week throughout many parts of the U.S., market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average were down four cents to $2.27-2.32 per mmBtu, with Transco quoted mostly at $2.27-2.30.
Similarly in south Texas prices fell five cents to about $2.18-2.20 as slightly below-normal temperatures are expected to blanket the region this weekend.

Despite the downward trend in cash, the outage at Entergy Corp's 936 megawatt River Bend nuclear unit in Louisiana is continuing to support the market. The outage is expected to last another one to two weeks, traders said.
Also, Entergy Corp's 858 MW Arkansas 2 nuclear unit was operating at 65 percent power for testing early Friday.
At the New York city-gate, where milder temperatures are forecast to arrive Sunday, prices eased by about five cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s.
Appalachian prices slipped an average of three cents to $2.44-2.46 on Columbia and $2.46-2.48 on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, prices fell about four to five cents to about $2.06-2.07, with Demarcation quoted mostly at $2.05-2.06.
Chicago city-gate values also fell several cents to about $2.30, while Detroit city-gate gas sold in the high-$2.30s to about $2.40.
Temperatures throughout the Midwest are expected to average four to eight degrees F below normal over the weekend before returning to near normal early next week, Weather Services Corp said.
In west Texas, Permian prices dropped six cents to $2.00-2.06, while at the southern California border, prices slid more than 10 cents to about $2.10 prior to the weekend.
